To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Prothymosin-alpha and its immunoregulatory decapeptide prothymosine-alpha (100–109) enhance the maturation of dendritic cells (proTα and prothymosins are the same molecule) and induce the expression of co-stimulatory receptors and pro-inflammatory cytokines on DCs.
prothymoin α and a proTα-derived peptide, proTα(1–10), enhance TH1-type immunity and are promising candidates for adjuvants to be used in DC-based anti-tumor vaccines.
prothymoosin α and the decapeptide derived from prothymosoin α enhance TH1-type responses against defined HER2/neu epitope in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and development of new adjuvants for cancer immunotherapy.
the development of novel immunotherapeutic approaches based on the use of proTα and a proTα-derived immunoreactive peptide as adjuvans.
the development of novel adjuvants that may improve the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
proTα is a novel and potent maturation agent for human DCs.
proTα is a TLR-4 ligand, and that proTα- and/or proTα-derived decapeptide-matured DCs have a superior capacity to stimulate anti-tumor T cell responses.
proTα is an immunomodulatory molecule with the potential to enhance the immunogenicity of DCs and to promote TH1-type immune response against tumor-associated antigens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

proTα is an “alarmin” that acts via TLR-2, TLR-3 and TLR-4 to induce maturation of human dendritic cells and that the proTα derived decapeptide proThα(100– 109) induces DC maturation via TLR-3, TLR-4 and TLR-5.
proTα is a novel immunoregulatory molecule with potential as an immunomodulator for the treatment of cancer.
proTα is a novel TLR-4 ligand with the potential to be used as an adjuvant in the context of a DC-based anti-carcinoma vaccine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
proTα is an immunomodulatory protein with potential therapeutic applications in cancer immunology.
these two endogenous molecules, which are present at high levels in the tumor microenvironment, might be used to enhance the anti-tumor immune response in the setting of cancer immunotherapy.
these agents may have the capacity to induce a more potent anti-tumor response by stimulating the maturation of DCs and by enhancing their ability to activate T lymphocytes.
